code: Options: on EXIT, press button B (the C key) 128 times
effect: A sound plays, EXIT turns into < EXIT >, and Left or Right on it opens a hidden DEBUG MODE page
note: Button B on EXIT counts presses in DS:468E (CS:C588); at 128 it sets the flag DS:468C, draws < EXIT > and plays effect $44. Holding the key works too, about 45 seconds. The count starts again each time the options open; the flag stays until a reset. Done on the unpatched disk in DOSBox-X with scripted C presses. The page behind it was opened on a copy with the flag already set (disk $1650C = 01).

code: Finish stage 9 with under 20 minutes on the clock
effect: A hidden 10th opponent, すーぱーたけ (Super Take), before the ending
note: When the next stage would be the 10th and the play time (the PAST TIME on the continue screen) is under 0:20:00, the game sets DS:4680 and plays stage index 9 instead of going to the ending (CS:703F). Its card reads STAGE 0. The opponent was seen through the debug page's STAGE SELECT 10; the 20-minute rule itself was read from the code, not played out.

code: Hold CTRL while the disk boots
effect: The game uses the 31 kHz display mode instead of 24 kHz
note: The boot code tests the CTRL bit of the BIOS key flags (CS:02EC) and picks the display mode from it. Read from the code; the not-held path (24 kHz) shows in the DOSBox-X log.

code: Hold A + B as a second player joins a 1P game
effect: The options screen opens before the VS game starts
note: After HERE COMES A NEW CHALLENGER !, if either player's input is exactly A + B the game runs the options screen first (CS:6F9A). Read from the code, not run.

effect: MODE (BOMBER SELECT, 21 RENSA, 5 RENSA * 2), STAGE SELECT 1-10, CHANCE TIME 1-5 MIN or NOTHING, DEKAB METER ZERO or MAX - 1
note: Opened with Left or Right on < EXIT > once the page is unlocked; < RETURN > goes back. MODE is read from the code only: BOMBER SELECT lets the player re-roll each piece with Up, and the two RENSA modes deal pieces from fixed lists that set up a 21-chain or two 5-chains (CS:B2A9, CS:B2CD). BOMBER SELECT didn't show in two runs. Page seen on a copy with the flag set.

effect: The 1P game starts at stage 3; 10 starts on the hidden opponent
note: The setting is the word DS:466C (0-9), read when the 1P game starts (CS:ED5F). Seen with the word preset to 2 on a copy of the disk (disk $164EC).

effect: CHANCE TIME !! comes after 1 minute of a match instead of 3
note: DS:466E, 1-5 minutes or NOTHING, default 3 (CS:AF91): the game as sold always uses 3 minutes. Seen with the word preset to 1 on a copy of the disk (disk $164EE): CHANCE TIME !! at 1m00s.

effect: Both giant-bomb meters start one step from full
note: DS:4670 (CS:BA1F). Seen with the word preset on a copy of the disk (disk $164F0).

effect: The DEBUG MODE page is unlocked from the start
note: The byte is the flag DS:468C in the disk image (DS:xxxx = disk $11E80 + xxxx). On a copy with it set, the options show < EXIT > at once and the page opens.

effect: Four boot messages in English that nothing prints, one of them for a copy-protection check the game doesn't have
note: DS:0800 (disk $12680): PANIC BOMBER, FOR FM PC9821, NOW LOADING... and PROTECT CHECK ERROR!!. The boot screen uses Japanese strings instead, and no protection check exists in the code. Also unreferenced: the id string Panibon For PC9821 (DS:9410) and the text titles CONFIGRATION and DEBUG MODE, since both pages' titles are part of their background pictures.

effect: A register dump and a memory viewer the developers left in, reached only if the game crashes
note: INT 3 prints the registers and waits for RETURN (CS:06AE). INT 0Dh opens a hex and ASCII memory viewer at the fault address (CS:0566: ROLL UP/DOWN scroll, ESC leaves), then prints Ippan Hogo!! (general protection) and stops. A text-console line input (CS:03D4) has no caller.
